nodes.name: ZIF-67 Nanocube Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 292 mg of Co(NO3)2·6H2O was dissolved in 10 ml of deionized water along with 4 mg of CTAB. Following this, the solution was quickly added to 70 mL of an aqueous mixture that included 4.54 g of 2-MIM and stirred for 40 minutes at ambient temperature. The final product was collected by centrifugation and thoroughly washed several times with ethanol.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of ZIF-67 nanocubes (NCs)... stirred for 40 minutes at ambient temperature.

nodes.name: Co-TA Complex Formation
nodes.procedure: Initially, 60 mg of ZIF-67 nanocubes (NCs) were dispersed in 20 ml of ethanol before being transferred into a solvent mixture comprising 300 ml of ethanol and DI water in a 1:1 volume ratio containing 1 mg mL⁻¹ of tannic acid (TA). The resulting mixture was stirred at room temperature for 10 minutes. Subsequently, the product was isolated via centrifugation and subjected to multiple ethanol washes. Finally, the product was dried in an oven at 60 °C.

unit_operations.name: Chemical Etching
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The resulting mixture was stirred at room temperature for 10 minutes.

nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Co-tannic acid complex nanoboxes (Co-TA NBs)... dried in an oven at 60 °C.

nodes.name: Co3O4 Nanobox Calcination
nodes.procedure: The Co-TA nanoboxes were subjected to annealing at 350 °C for 3 hours, with the temperature increasing at a rate of 1 °C per minute in air, followed by natural cooling to room temperature.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Co3O4 NBs... annealing at 350 °C for 3 hours... in air.

nodes.name: Ru-Co3O4 Cation Exchange and Calcination
nodes.procedure: 50 mg of Co-TA NBs was dispersed into 10 ml of ethanol. Subsequently, 4 mL DI water containing 10 mM RuCl3·xH2O was added dropwise to the aforementioned dispersion, which was then stirred at room temperature for 3 h. The resultant product was harvested via centrifugation, subsequently washed multiple times with ethanol, and finally dried in an oven at 70 °C. The obtained powder was placed in a tube furnace and heated at 350 °C for 3 h with a heating rate of 1 °C min⁻¹ in air.

nodes.characterization_summary: WAXS confirms decreased yet retained spinel crystalline structure in Ru-Co₃O₄ post single atom incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Wide-angle X-ray scattering (WAXS) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns confirm the decreased yet retained spinel crystalline structure in Ru-Co₃O₄ post single atom incorporation (Fig. 1b, Supplementary Figs. 4 and 5).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm retained spinel crystalline structure in Ru-Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Wide-angle X-ray scattering (WAXS) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns confirm the decreased yet retained spinel crystalline structure in Ru-Co₃O₄ post single atom incorporation (Fig. 1b, Supplementary Figs. 4 and 5).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanobox hollow structure of Ru-Co₃O₄ with 10 nm wall thickness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images vividly illustrate the nanobox hollow structure of Ru-Co₃O₄ with a 10 nm wall thickness (Fig. 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals lattice fringe of 0.29 nm assigned to (220) plane of Co₃O₄ with notable crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) reveals a lattice fringe of 0.29 nm with notable crystallinity, which can be assigned to the (220) plane of Co₃O₄ (Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows Ru single atoms anchored in Co₃O₄ matrix with even elemental distribution throughout hollow nanobox structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) elemental mapping demonstrates an even distribution of elements throughout the hollow nanobox structure (Fig. 1e). HAADF-STEM images showcase Ru single atoms anchored in the Co₃O₄ matrix (Fig. 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT of Ru K-edge EXAFS shows peaks at 1.5 Å and 2.5 Å attributed to Ru-O and Ru-O-Ru/Co coordinations; Ru-O coordination number of 6.2 confirms octahedral site occupancy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transforms (FT) of the Ru K-edge EXAFS spectra unveil two prominent peaks at 1.5 Å and 2.5 Å for Ru-Co₃O₄, attributed to Ru-O and Ru-O-Ru/Co coordinations, respectively (Fig. 2a). Quantitative EXAFS fitting results demonstrate a Ru-O coordination number of 6.2 (Fig. 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES determines Ru valence state of +3.7 in Ru-Co₃O₄, lower than in RuO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Utilizing XANES spectroscopy, the valence state of Ru in Ru-Co₃O₄ is determined to be +3.7, lower than in RuO₂ (Fig. 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: WT analysis shows maxima at 4.3 Å⁻¹ (Ru-O) and 6.8 Å⁻¹ (Ru-O-Co), absence of 9.0 Å⁻¹ peak confirms no RuO₂ clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru-O-Co and Ru-O coordinations are shown at 6.8 Å⁻¹ and 4.3 Å⁻¹, respectively (Fig. 2c). However, no maximum at 9.0 Å⁻¹ denoting the Ru-O-Ru bridge structure has been found.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge EXAFS shows Co-O peak shift from 1.52 Å in Co₃O₄ to 1.49 Å in Ru-Co₃O₄ indicating 2% local compressive strain.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co-O coordination peak at 1.52 Å in Co₃O₄ shifts negatively to 1.49 Å in Ru-Co₃O₄, indicating a 2% local compressive strain on Co-O bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: O K-edge XANES shows decreased unoccupied O 2p-Co 3d hybridized state (~530 eV) in Ru-Co₃O₄ indicating heightened charge accumulation on O species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the O K-edge XANES, a conspicuous decrease in the unoccupied O 2p-Co 3d hybridized state (~530 eV; peak a) was evident in Ru-Co₃O₄ compared to Co₃O₄ (Fig. 2f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES shows heightened Co valence state in Ru-Co₃O₄ compared to Co₃O₄, evidenced by adsorption edge shift to higher energy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further XANES analysis demonstrates a heightened Co valence state in Ru-Co₃O₄ compared to Co₃O₄, evidenced by the shift of the adsorption edge to higher energy (Supplementary Fig. 15a).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ru 3p peaks at 463.6 eV and 486.1 eV; Co 2p₃/₂ peak at 779.8 eV shifted +0.18 eV indicating increased Co oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru 3p region XPS spectrum displays two prominent peaks at 463.6 eV (Ru 3p₃/₂) and 486.1 eV (Ru 3p₁/₂) for Ru-Co₃O₄... the Co 2p₃/₂ XPS peak at 779.8 eV for Co³⁺ in Ru-Co₃O₄ demonstrates a 0.18 eV positive shift.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Co K-edge EXAFS shows minimal coordination structure changes and structural robustness of Ru-Co₃O₄ during OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Operando EXAFS and quantitative analyses reveal subtle changes in the coordination environment of Co elements as potential varies... indicating the structural robustness of Ru-Co₃O₄ under OER conditions.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Ru K-edge EXAFS shows Ru-O bond compression from 1.52 Å at OCP to 1.49 Å at 1.03 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Operando EXAFS analyses at the Ru K-edge reveal a predominant peak of Ru-O at 1.52 Å at OCP... This peak shifts negatively to 1.49 Å at a potential of 1.03 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms Ru content of 4.49 wt% in the Ru-Co₃O₄ sample used for main characterizations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Characterization results of Ru-Co₃O₄ sample shown in Figs. 1 and 2 are based on the sample with a Ru content of 4.49 wt%.
